documentation: Custom domains are claimed per-repo via a CNAME file; an unclaimed github.io target serves the canonical 'There isn't a GitHub Pages site here' 404, and anyone can create the repo that claims it.
herokuapp.com wildcards; a deleted/released app's name can be registered by anyone and the router serves 'No such app' until then.

herokudns.com targets have no wildcard: when the app is gone the CNAME target itself is NXDOMAIN. Re-registering an app with the matching name claims the domain. No HTTP body fingerprint exists (the name stops resolving) — verify by attempting to claim.

S3 resolves bucket names via the Host header; if the bucket named by the CNAME doesn't exist, anyone can create a bucket with that name in any region and serve content on the domain. Covers .s3.amazonaws.com, .s3-website-<region>..., .s3.<region>..., .s3.dualstack....
azurewebsites.net wildcards; deleting an app frees the name and any new app with the same name re-claims the custom domain (page shows '404 Web Site not found.').
azureedge.net endpoints are historically claimable by re-registering the endpoint name. No stable public body fingerprint on record — confirm by attempting to claim the endpoint name.
cloudapp.azure.com / cloudapp.net have no wildcard: an unclaimed deployment means the CNAME target itself is NXDOMAIN; re-deploying a cloud service with the same name claims the DNS name.
Like S3: bucket name comes from the Host header, so a dangling CNAME to a non-existent bucket can be claimed by creating a GCS bucket with that name (body returns NoSuchBucket).

http_fingerprint: sorry, this shop is currently unavailable
documentation: Dangling myshopify.com custom-domain CNAMEs serve 'Sorry, this shop is currently unavailable'; the shop name can be re-registered (Shopify support arbitration handles contested claims).
Fastly serves 'Fastly error: unknown domain' when the domain isn't mapped to any service; adding the domain to your own Fastly service claims it (edge case: some accounts need Fastly approval).

Netlify serves a 'Not Found - Request ID' page for domains not attached to a site; the custom domain can be registered onto a new Netlify site (Netlify verifies via DNS record, which the attacker does not control — historically claimable).

Unclaimed vercel.app / vercel-dns targets return DEPLOYMENT_NOT_FOUND / 404: NOT_FOUND. Edge case: Vercel requires the domain's DNS to point at your account before accepting it — verify claimability before reporting.
bitbucket.io sites are repo-backed; a deleted repo/ account leaves the domain serving 'Repository not found' and any new repo with the same name claims it.

http_fingerprint: the thing you were looking for is no longer here
documentation: Ghost(Pro) custom domains: cancelled publications leave the domain on Ghost's error page ('The thing you were looking for is no longer here'), and the subdomain can be re-registered on a new Ghost(Pro) trial.

http_fingerprint: the gods are wise, but do not know of the site which you seek
documentation: Deleted Pantheon site environments free the pantheonsite.io name; a new site with the same name re-claims custom domains pointed at it (page: 'The gods are wise, but do not know of the site which you seek.').

Deleted/trial-expired Zendesk accounts free the subdomain; the 'Help Center Closed' page marks the dangling state. Modern Zendesk requires account verification before some names — verify claimability.
Custom domains on Tumblr map to <name>.tumblr.com; when that blog is gone the page reads '...doesn't currently exist at this address' and the name can be re-registered on a new Tumblr blog.
Surge.sh static hosting: 'project not found' means the project name is free and anyone can publish a new project under that exact name, claiming the domain.

An unclaimed Statuspage custom domain redirects to the Statuspage marketing site (Rails-style 'You are being ... statuspage.io ... redirected' body). Registering a new Statuspage account with that domain claims it.
Readme.io docs projects: deleted/unregistered project names show 'Project doesnt exist... yet!' and can be created again, claiming custom domains pointed at readme.io.

http_fingerprint: this uservoice subdomain is currently available
documentation: UserVoice literally serves 'This UserVoice subdomain is currently available!' for unclaimed subdomains — the clearest vendor-admitted takeover state.

http_fingerprint: we could not find what you
documentation: HelpJuice knowledge-base custom domains: unclaimed/deleted accounts serve the HelpJuice 404 ('We could not find what you're looking for'); the subdomain can be re-registered.

http_fingerprint: no settings were found for this company
documentation: helpscoutdocs.com doc sites: 'No settings were found for this company' marks the dangling state; registering a Docs site with that subdomain claims it.

http_fingerprint: this page is reserved for artistic dogs
documentation: Intercom custom help centers: unregistered custom domains serve the 'This page is reserved for artistic dogs' 404; adding the domain to a new Intercom env claims it.
Unregistered *.wordpress.com subdomains serve a WordPress.com page asking 'Do you want to register ...?' — the name can be claimed via a new WordPress.com blog (edge case: some names are reserved).

http_fingerprint: the requested url was not found on this server
documentation: Unbounce landing pages use <name>.unbouncepages.com CNAMEs (bare .unbounce.com is the vendor root — rare); unclaimed pages serve a plain Apache 404 — generic string, corroborate manually before reporting.
webflow.io project subdomains for removed/unpublished projects serve a Webflow 404. Vendor response text has changed over time — treat matches as leads and verify claimability manually.
Teamwork.com project sites: deleted projects leave the subdomain on a 'Oops - We couldn't find that page' 404; historically re-registrable.

http_fingerprint: maybe this page moved, deleted, or is nowhere to be found
documentation: Freshdesk support portals: deleted/unclaimed portals serve a Freshdesk 404; the subdomain can be registered on a new Freshdesk account (support arbitration may apply).
Wufoo form subdomains are historically takeover-prone after account deletion. No stable body fingerprint pinned here — verify manually by attempting to register the subdomain.
Campaign Monitor (createsend.com) hosted pages: unclaimed accounts serve a page containing 'Trying to access your account?'; re-creating the account claims the subdomain.
Cargo sites: the documented fingerprint is a bare generic '404 Not Found' — too generic to automate safely. Verify manually via the Cargo custom-domain flow.
Acquia-hosted Drupal sites: deleted environments free acquia-sites.com names. No stable public body fingerprint pinned here — verify manually.

Historically claimable via reserved tunnel names ('Tunnel <name>.ngrok.io not found'). Modern ngrok plans restrict arbitrary claiming — verify before reporting. ERR_NGROK_3200 confirmed as ngrok's current error code for this state (DNSReaper punk-security/dnsReaper, cross-checked against ngrok's own error-code docs).
Deleted Fly.io apps free fly.dev names; response text has changed across versions. Verify manually by attempting to allocate the app hostname.

Deleted Elastic Beanstalk environments free their <env>.<region>.elasticbeanstalk.com CNAME target; the target itself goes NXDOMAIN (no wildcard). Classic, long-documented takeover class (originally in EdOverflow/can-i-take-over-xyz) — no HTTP fingerprint applies since the target doesn't resolve; verify by attempting to launch an environment with the matching name in the matching region.
AgileCRM landing-page custom domains: unclaimed targets serve 'No landing page found.' Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/agilecrm.py).
Aha.io product-portal custom domains: unclaimed portals serve an 'invalid-portal' page. Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/aha.py).

Airee.ru (Russian video-hosting CDN) custom domains: unclaimed targets serve a Russian-language 'Error 402. Airee.rf service is not enabled' page. Niche/regional service, keep verification manual. Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/airee_ru.py).

http_fingerprint: is not registered as whitelabel or custom domain
documentation: Brandpad.io brand-guideline sites: unclaimed custom domains serve 'is not registered as whitelabel or custom domain.' Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/brandpad.py).

Frontify brand-portal custom domains: unclaimed targets serve a branded '404 - Not Found - Frontify' page (service name in the error text — strong signal). Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/frontify.py).

GetResponse landing-page (gr8.com) custom domains: unclaimed targets serve 'is no longer available.' Generic-sounding message — corroborate manually before reporting. Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/getresponse.py).

JetBrains-hosted YouTrack custom domains: an unconfigured/deleted instance's CNAME target serves the generic 'YouTrack Starting Page' (i.e. no specific project bound to that hostname yet). Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/jetbrains.py).

http_fingerprint: it looks like you may have taken a wrong turn somewhere
documentation: LaunchRock pre-launch landing pages: unclaimed targets serve 'It looks like you may have taken a wrong turn somewhere.' Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/launchrock_cname.py).
Mashery (TIBCO) API-portal custom domains: unclaimed targets serve 'Unrecognized domain.' Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/mashery.py).
MySmartJobBoard custom domains: unclaimed job-board targets serve 'Job Board Is Unavailable.' Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/mysmartjobboard.py).

http_fingerprint: this domain is not configured on short.io
documentation: Short.io custom link-shortener domains: unclaimed targets serve 'This domain is not configured on Short.io.' (service name in the error text — strong signal). Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/short.py).

http_fingerprint: the link to this simplebooklet may have changed
documentation: Simplebooklet custom domains: unclaimed targets serve 'The link to this Simplebooklet may have changed' (service name in the error text — strong signal). Note: this repo's original entry for Simplebooklet had no fingerprint on record; this supersedes it. Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/simplebooklet.py).
Wishpond landing-page custom domains: unclaimed targets redirect/serve a link back to wishpond.com's own 404 page. Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/wishpond.py).

AnnounceKit changelog-widget custom domains: DNSReaper detects the unclaimed state by HTTP status code rather than a stable body string — no fingerprint pinned here, verify manually. Source: DNSReaper (punk-security/dnsReaper, signatures/announcekit.py).
